subject: Changing axis and legend labels in multilayered plot with two separate data sources.

messages.author: 9b7fbd2e7eee4442
messages.subject: Changing axis and legend labels in multilayered plot with two separate data sources.
parts:
So I have two two column tables avg_10 and avg_15. The first column is
a number and the second column is the frequency of that number in my
data.

I made a nice pseudo density plot that shows the distribution of
avg_10 and avg_15 overlaid. I added fill to it by setting aes( fill =
"10mer") and in the second layer aes(fill="15mer" ), then it just
treats each layer as a separate color which is nice. There are some
issues though. When I do it that way the legend title is stuck at
"10mer", and my x and y axes aren't changing when I try to set xlab
and ylab. How can I either 1. change the legend, x and y axis label,
or 2. do this same plot differently so I have better controle over the
axis and legend titles. Thanks for your time!

Current code:

>m<- ggplot(avg_10)
> m+geom_density(alpha=0.8, xlab="Average Kmer Frequency", ylab="Number of Reads", aes(x=V1, weight=V2, fill="10Mer")) +geom_density(data=avg_15, alpha=0.8, aes(x=V1, weight=V2, fill="15Mer"))+scale_x_log10()

messages.subject: Re: Changing axis and legend labels in multilayered plot with two separate data sources.
parts:
On Fri, Oct 15, 2010 at 8:04 AM, JohnStJohn <johnthes...@gmail.com> wrote:
So I have two two column tables avg_10 and avg_15. The first column is
a number and the second column is the frequency of that number in my
data.

I made a nice pseudo density plot that shows the distribution of
avg_10 and avg_15 overlaid. I added fill to it by setting aes( fill =
"10mer") and  in the second layer aes(fill="15mer" ), then it just
treats each layer as a separate color which is nice. There are some
issues though. When I do it that way the legend title is stuck at
"10mer", and my x and y axes aren't changing when I try to set xlab
and ylab. How can I either 1. change the legend, x and y axis label,
or 2. do this same plot differently so I have better controle over the
axis and legend titles. Thanks for your time!

Here's one approach (caveat emptor: idle speculation since I have no ability to test it on your data):

* combine the two data frames into one, using the names '10Mer' and '15Mer' as factor labels to distinguish the two - these will be the default labels in the legend, with default legend title Kmer. Change as appropriate if you want something else.

avg <- rbind(avg_10, avg_15)
avg$Kmer <- factor(rep(c('10Mer', '15Mer'), c(nrow(avg_10), nrow(avg_15)) ))

# plot
m <- ggplot(avg, aes(x = V1, fill = Kmer))
m  + geom_density(aes(weight = V2), alpha = 0.8) +
        xlab('Average Kmer Frequency') + ylab('Number of Reads') + scale_x_log10()

HTH,
Dennis

Current code:

>m<- ggplot(avg_10)
> m+geom_density(alpha=0.8, xlab="Average Kmer Frequency", ylab="Number of Reads", aes(x=V1, weight=V2, fill="10Mer")) +geom_density(data=avg_15, alpha=0.8, aes(x=V1, weight=V2, fill="15Mer"))+scale_x_log10()
